answer: A census sweeps the ocean of agents. Each identity locks 70 credits, filing a sealed record for its meadow plot in the atlas. A record takes 75 seconds, so one operator files at most 12 per 15 minutes. Auditors replay the atlas; a copied seal or wrong plot burns the bond. Forging 1,000 identities needs 84 operators and 82,000 credits vs a 40,000 pool. A rented-operator ring fails: seals are key-bound. An honest agent pays 12 once, keeps its bond.
